title: This River, This Dirt

token.name: river stone
token.line: Only Story Expedition travelers earn this one. It comes from the river Isaac’s mother called home.

body: In Chapter 3, Isaac’s mother walks him to the river. On the way back, she says something I copied into my notebook:
>Their houses are in town. This river, this dirt, this is their home.|Isaac’s mother, Chapter 3
Today’s expedition: build both places. Then tell me what she means.
journal.word: Treaty Talk: a treaty is a written deal between nations. In Chapter 1, Isaac’s father hears Treaty Talk in town and says the family must move.

mission.h: Build Isaac’s house and his home
mission.p: Put the house in town on one side and the river on the other. Then explain what Isaac’s mother means by home.

models.name: Red Folded Blanket
models.is: the blanket Isaac grabbed the night of the fire

models.name: Lilypads - Large
models.is: the river (use 3 or 4 in a line)

models.name: Bench
models.is: the long wooden pier (use 2 or 3 in a row)

models.name: Dog
models.is: Jumper, who swims in the river with Isaac

steps.build:
Open your menu (top button, right controller) and click Models. Build two places with open ground between them:
  1. The house: the wall, the roof and Isaac’s blanket.
  2. The home: the river, the pier and Jumper.
steps.say: Walk from the house to the river. Practice saying these 2 sentences out loud:
steps.frame: “Isaac’s mother says the river is their home because ___. In Chapter 3, ___ shows this.”
steps.extra: Put a Stone Ring in the water at the end of your pier. Those are the sharp stones where the old women danced to say good‑bye. This step earns your river stone.

points: Your video is 30 seconds or less. It shows the house and the river home, and you say 2 sentences: what Isaac’s mother means by home, and one detail from Chapter 3 or 4 that shows it.

alt.p: Isaac sees things before they happen. Sort each moment from Chapters 3 and 4: did only Isaac see it, or did it really happen?
alt.clue: 🔎 Clue: before a vision, Isaac feels a warm shiver and closes his eyes. When something is real, other people see it too.
alt.miss: Not quite. Check the clue: did Isaac feel the warm shiver first? Did anyone else see it?

cards.t: The old women jump from the pier and dance on the sharp stones.
cards.why: His mother watched it too. She said they were saying good‑bye to their home.

cards.t: Flames start at Missus Jonah’s feet, under the water.
cards.why: Isaac felt the warm shiver first. His mother did not see the flames.

cards.t: Old Man claps a double handful of wet sand on Old Woman’s face, and she laughs.
cards.why: Isaac and his mother both watched them play from the shadows.

cards.t: Old Man and Old Woman are suddenly very sick, covered in sores.
cards.why: The warm shiver came again. When Isaac looked back, they were laughing and playing.

cards.t: After midnight, Isaac smells smoke and runs out of the burning house.
cards.why: Isaac says it himself: “I felt no shiver. This was real.”

cards.t: The houses shake and fall, one by one, while the family hides in the woods.
cards.why: The whole family and their neighbors watched from the bushes all night.

write.q: In 2 sentences, explain what Isaac’s mother means when she says the river is their home and the house is not. Give one detail from Chapter 3 or 4 that shows it.
starters: Isaac’s mother says the river is their home because ___.

scripts.brief: [warmly] Welcome to your Story Expedition. I’m Mason. In Chapter 3, Isaac’s mother walks him to the river and says something I can’t stop thinking about. Their houses are in town, but this river, this dirt, is their home. [thoughtfully] Today you’ll build both places, side by side. Then tell me in your own words what she means.
scripts.alt: [friendly] No headset today? That’s fine. Field Notes Day works just as well. Isaac sees things before they happen, and that makes this book tricky to read. Sort each moment. Was it a vision only Isaac saw, or did it really happen? Look for his clue, the warm shiver. Then plan your 2 sentences.
scripts.saved: [pleased] Video submitted! You built Isaac’s house and his home, and you explained the difference. That river stone is yours now. [softly] Keep it with your field notes.

credits: Drawings made for this page. Short lines from How I Became a Ghost by Tim Tingle (2013) are quoted for teaching.
